title: Dasakam 97 — Uttamabhaktiprārthanā tathā Mārkaṇḍeya Kathā
description: A prayer for steadfast devotion followed by the story of Mārkaṇḍeya: his service, long austerity, vision of the infant on the banyan leaf, and the Lord’s revelation of the worlds and Vaikuṇṭha.
translation_note: No vetted English verse translation is present in the supplied source bundle; translation_en remains intentionally empty pending editorial review. The supplied photos have no per-photo descriptive captions. The chapter commentary field contains studio paraphrases of the canonical Sanskrit stanzas, not source captions or translations credited to anyone.

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्रैगुण्याद्भिन्नरूपं भवति हि भुवने हीनमध्योत्तमं यत्
ज्ञानं श्रद्धा च कर्ता वसतिरपि सुखं कर्म चाहारभेदाः ।
त्वत् क्षेत्रत्वन्निषेवादि तु यदिह पुनस्त्वत्परं तत्तु सर्वं
प्राहुर्नैर्गुण्यनिष्ठं तदनुभजनतो मङ्क्षु सिद्धो भवेयम् ॥ ९७-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The world’s knowledge, faith, actions, dwellings, joys, and foods differ through the three qualities. What is centered on You and Your service is described as established beyond those qualities; by worshipping You, may I quickly attain that state.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
traiguṇyādbhinnarūpaṃ bhavati hi bhuvane hīnamadhyottamaṃ yat
jñānaṃ śraddhā ca kartā vasatirapi sukhaṃ karma cāhārabhedāḥ |
tvat kṣetratvanniṣevādi tu yadiha punastvatparaṃ tattu sarvaṃ
prāhurnairguṇyaniṣṭhaṃ tadanubhajanato maṅkṣu siddho bhaveyam || 97-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वय्येव न्यस्तचित्तः सुखमयि विचरन् सर्वचेष्टास्त्वदर्थं
त्वद्भक्तैः सेव्यमानानपि चरितचरानाश्रयन् पुण्यदेशान् ।
दस्यौ विप्रे मृगादिष्वपि च सममतिर्मुच्यमानावमान-
स्पर्धासूयादिदोषः सततमखिलभूतेषु सम्पूजये त्वाम् ॥ ९७-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: May I keep my mind on You, make every action an offering, and seek the sacred places served by Your devotees. Free of contempt, rivalry, and envy, may I honor You continually in every being, seeing a thief, a Brahmin, and animals with equal regard.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvayyeva nyastacittaḥ sukhamayi vicaran sarvaceṣṭāstvadarthaṃ
tvadbhaktaiḥ sevyamānānapi caritacarānāśrayan puṇyadeśān |
dasyau vipre mṛgādiṣvapi ca samamatirmucyamānāvamāna-
spardhāsūyādidoṣaḥ satatamakhilabhūteṣu sampūjaye tvām || 97-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वद्भावो यावदेषु स्फुरति न विशदं तावदेवं ह्युपास्तिं
कुर्वन्नैकात्म्यबोधे झटिति विकसति त्वन्मयोऽहं चरेयम् ।
त्वद्धर्मस्यास्य तावत् किमपि न भगवन् प्रस्तुतस्य प्रणाश-
-स्तस्मात् सर्वात्मनैव प्रदिश मम विभो भक्तिमार्गं मनोज्ञम् ॥ ९७-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: While Your presence is not yet clearly seen in all things, let me worship in this way; through the insight of oneness may I become filled with You and move through life accordingly. Since this path of devotion is not to be abandoned, Lord, grant me the beautiful way of devotion with all my being.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvadbhāvo yāvadeṣu sphurati na viśadaṃ tāvadevaṃ hyupāstiṃ
kurvannaikātmyabodhe jhaṭiti vikasati tvanmayo’haṃ careyam |
tvaddharmasyāsya tāvat kimapi na bhagavan prastutasya praṇāśa-
-stasmāt sarvātmanaiva pradiśa mama vibho bhaktimārgaṃ manojñam || 97-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
तं चैनं भक्तियोगं द्रढयितुमयि मे साध्यमारोग्यमायु-
-दिष्ट्या तत्रापि सेव्यं तव चरणमहो भेषजायेव दुग्धम् ।
मार्कण्डेयो हि पूर्वं गणकनिगदितद्वादशाब्दायुरुच्चैः
सेवित्वा वत्सरं त्वां तव भटनिवहैर्द्रावयामास मृत्युम् ॥ ९७-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: To strengthen this devotion, I need health and a long life; may Your feet be served as a remedy, like milk. Mārkaṇḍeya, once said by an astrologer to have only twelve years, served You for a year, and Your attendants drove Death away.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
taṃ cainaṃ bhaktiyogaṃ draḍhayitumayi me sādhyamārogyamāyu-
-rdiṣṭyā tatrāpi sevyaṃ tava caraṇamaho bheṣajāyeva dugdham |
mārkaṇḍeyo hi pūrvaṃ gaṇakanigaditadvādaśābdāyurccaiḥ
sevitvā vatsaraṃ tvāṃ tava bhaṭanivahairdrāvayāmāsa mṛtyum || 97-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
मार्कण्डेयश्चिरायुः स खलु पुनरपि त्वत्परः पुष्पभद्रा-
-तीरे निन्ये तपस्यन्नतुलसुखरतिः षट् तु मन्वन्तराणि ।
देवेन्द्रः सप्तमस्तं सुरयुवतिमरुन्मन्मथैर्मोहयिष्यन्
योगोष्मप्लुष्यमाणैर्न तु पुनरशकत्त्वज्जनं निर्जयेत् कः ॥ ९७-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Mārkaṇḍeya lived long and remained devoted to You, practicing austerity on the Pushpabhadrā for six manvantaras with incomparable joy. Indra, the seventh, sent celestial women, wind, and Kāma to distract him, but the heat of his yoga overcame their attempt; who could defeat one devoted to You?
stanzas.stanza_roman:
mārkaṇḍeyaścirāyuḥ sa khalu punarapi tvatparaḥ puṣpabhadrā-
-tīre ninye tapasyannatulasukharatiḥ ṣaṭ tu manvantarāṇi |
devendraḥ saptamastaṃ surayuvatimarunmanmathairmohayiṣyan
yogoṣmapluṣyamāṇairna tu punaraśakattvajjanaṃ nirjayet kaḥ || 97-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
प्रीत्या नारायणाख्यस्त्वमथ नरसखः प्राप्तवानस्य पार्श्वं
तुष्ट्या तोष्टूयमानः स तु विविधवरैर्लोभितो नानुमेने ।
द्रष्टुं मायां त्वदीयां किल पुनरवृणोद्भक्तितृप्तान्तरात्मा
मायादुःखानभिज्ञस्तदपि मृगयते नूनमाश्चर्यहेतोः ॥ ९७-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: You, known as Nārāyaṇa and companion of Nara, joyfully came to Mārkaṇḍeya. Though offered many boons, he declined them, content in devotion; he chose instead to see Your māyā out of wonder, though he knew nothing of its suffering.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
prītyā nārāyaṇākhyastvamatha narasakhaḥ prāptavānasya pārśvaṃ
tuṣṭyā toṣṭūyamānaḥ sa tu vividhavarairlobhito nānumene |
draṣṭuṃ māyāṃ tvadīyāṃ kila punaravṛṇodbhaktitṛptāntarātmā
māyāduḥkhānabhijñastadapi mṛgayate nūnamāścaryahetoḥ || 97-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
याते त्वय्याशु वाताकुलजलदगलत्तोयपूर्णातिघूर्णत्
सप्तार्णोराशिमग्ने जगति स तु जले सम्भ्रमन् वर्षकोटीः ।
दीनः प्रैक्षिष्ट दूरे वटदलशयनं कञ्चिदाश्चर्यबालं
त्वामेव श्यामलाङ्गं वदनसरसिजन्यस्तपादाङ्गुलीकम् ॥ ९७-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: After You departed, storms poured water from the clouds and the world sank beneath the churning seven oceans; Mārkaṇḍeya wandered helplessly through the waters for countless years. In the distance he saw a wondrous infant, dark blue like You, resting on a banyan leaf with its toes near its lotus mouth.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
yāte tvayyāśu vātākulajaladagalattoyapūrṇātighūrṇat
saptārṇorāśimagne jagati sa tu jale sambhraman varṣakoṭīḥ |
dīnaḥ praikṣiṣṭa dūre vaṭadalaśayanaṃ kañcidāścaryabālaṃ
tvāmeva śyāmalāṅgaṃ vadanasarasijanyastapādāṅgulīkam || 97-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वा त्वां हृष्टरोमा त्वरितमुपगतः स्प्रष्टुकामो मुनीन्द्रः
श्वासेनान्तर्निविष्टः पुनरिह सकलं दृष्टवान् विष्टपौघम् ।
भूयोऽपि श्वासवातैर्बहिरनुपतितो वीक्षितस्त्वत्कटाक्षै-
-र्मोदादाश्लेष्टुकामस्त्वयि पिहिततनौ स्वाश्रमे प्राग्वदासीत् ॥ ९७-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Thrilled, the sage hurried toward You to touch You, but entered within through the infant’s breath and saw the whole expanse of worlds there. Cast out again by the breath and met by Your loving glance, he reached to embrace You; You disappeared, and he found himself back in his hermitage as before.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
dṛṣṭvā tvāṃ hṛṣṭaromā tvaritamupagataḥ spraṣṭukāmo munīndraḥ
śvāsenāntarniviṣṭaḥ punariha sakalaṃ dṛṣṭavān viṣṭapaugham |
bhūyo’pi śvāsavātairbahiranupatito vīkṣitastvatkaṭākṣai-
-rmodādāśleṣṭukāmastvayi pihitatanau svāśrame prāgvadāsīt || 97-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
गौर्या सार्धं तदग्रे पुरभिदथ गतस्त्वत्प्रियप्रेक्षणार्थी
सिद्धानेवास्य दत्त्वा स्वयमयमजरामृत्युतादीन् गतोऽभूत् ।
एवं त्वत्सेवयैव स्मररिपुरपि स प्रीयते येन तस्मा-
-न्मूर्तित्रय्यात्मकस्त्वं ननु सकलनियन्तेति सुव्यक्तमासीत् ॥ ९७-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Shiva, the foe of Tripura, came there with Gauri, wishing to see Your beloved devotee. He granted Mārkaṇḍeya attainments including freedom from old age and death, then departed; because even Shiva delights in service to You, it became clear that You embody the three divine forms and govern all.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
gauryā sārdhaṃ tadagre purabhidatha gatastvatpriyaprekṣaṇārthī
siddhānevāsya dattvā svayam ayam ajarāmṛtyutādīn gato’bhūt |
evaṃ tvatsevayaiva smararipurapi sa prīyate yena tasmā-
-nmūrtitrayyātmakastvaṃ nanu sakalaniyanteti suvyaktamāsīt || 97-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्र्यंशेऽस्मिन् सत्यलोके विधिहरिपुरभिन्मन्दिराण्यूर्ध्वमूर्ध्वं
तेभ्योऽप्यूर्ध्वं तु मायाविकृतिविरहितो भाति वैकुण्ठलोकः ।
तत्र त्वं कारणाम्भस्यपि पशुपकुले शुद्धसत्त्वैकरूपी
सच्चिद्ब्रह्माद्वयात्मा पवनपुरपते पाहि मां सर्वरोगात् ॥ ९७-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Above the three worlds and the abodes of Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva shines Vaikuṇṭha, untouched by transformations of māyā. There You abide as pure being in the causal waters and among the cowherd folk, the nondual reality of existence and consciousness; Lord of Guruvayur, protect me from every illness.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tryaṃśe’smin satyaloke vidhiharipurabhinmandirāṇyūrdhvamūrdhvaṃ
tebhyo’pyūrdhvaṃ tu māyāvikṛtivirahito bhāti vaikuṇṭhalokaḥ |
tatra tvaṃ kāraṇāmbhasyapi paśupakule śuddhasattvaikarūpī
saccidbrahmādvayātmā pavanapurapate pāhi māṃ sarvarogāt || 97-10 ||
